text: In times of crises, it is important for people from all walks of life to band together and help one another.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: There are many threats beyond an actual armed conflict that could undermine a society's ability to be resilient and remain united.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Disruption to essential services can incite widespread fear and panic.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Disinformation campaigns have the potential to ignite societal divisions, wear at our social fabric and erode people's trust in the Government.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And, as we have seen in the past few years, a pandemic can erupt quite suddenly, disrupting our way of life.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The events in the past few years have been a sobering reminder that threats can arise from anywhere and that we cannot rely on the military alone to deal with them.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: A strong military is a necessary but insufficient component of our Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: To thrive, Singapore needs to invest in and build up a united, resilient society.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This concept involves every Singaporean playing their part to build our nation – which is critical in periods of difficulty.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: While we all hope that a crisis does not befall Singapore, we need to prepare for it nonetheless.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Given the ongoing conflicts in other parts of the world and the increasing prevalence of new frontiers of conflict and non-traditional threats, I would like to ask MINDEF – what Total Defence lessons we can we take away from these developments; and what MINDEF is planning to do in relation to Total Defence in the coming year?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This year, we commemorate the 40th anniversary of Total Defence.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are very fortunate to have had decades of peace and prosperity, but we should never take this for granted.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Eighty years ago, during the Japanese Occupation, Singapore experienced the horrors of war and suffered extreme privation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It was also a period when remarkable bravery and resilience shone through.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singapore is determined to be well-prepared for self-defence against future aggressions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Forty years ago, around the time the concept of Total Defence was introduced, the world split into two distinct blocs through the Cold War, with the threat of open conflict ever-present on the horizon.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Today, we must be cognisant of the fact that the prospect of conflict, no matter how small, always exists.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One needs only to look at the Russia-Ukraine war, which shows no signs of ending, and the Israel-Hamas conflict.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Even though both are far from our shores, they each have had significant impact on the world we live in and on our lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Total Defence is an important concept for all of Singapore society to coalesce around, especially in times of crises.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Every Singaporean must play our part: as individuals and as part of our community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As we celebrate 40 years of Total Defence, we must ensure that the concept remains relevant and resonant for all Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would therefore, like to ask MINDEF to provide an update on how the 40th anniversary of Total Defence is being commemorated and how do we ensure that Total Defence continues to remain relevant and important?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, I had briefly mentioned in my earlier cut about the insecurity of our global operating environment that has spurred many governments to invest in defence.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another important issue that I would like to elaborate on is about the preparedness of our people in times of such uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I spoke on the topic of civic preparedness through Total Defence during my cut for last year's Committee of Supply debate and I think it is timely to revisit this topic.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to enhance Singapore's readiness and build our nation's resilience to cope with potential crises and disruptions.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In his message, he said that the most critical factor in upholding our security is the determination and will of our people; and that all of us have a part to play to defend Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How would MINDEF heighten public awareness and increase participation of our civilians in regular preparation exercises?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How will MINDEF ensure that as many Singaporeans as possible, equip themselves with the necessary knowledge and skills to cope with potential disruptions and attacks?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, our NSmen play a significant role in Singapore's defence.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Our men put their career aspirations on hold for two years and after NS, they continue to serve as Operationally Ready National Service (ORNS) duties.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Balancing NS along with professional and personal obligations poses new challenges as they enter the workforce and even more competing pressures as they start families.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: All of us, including our employers, must play our part in ensuring that our NSmen feel supported and recognised for their activities and sacrifices.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: My question for MINDEF is: what role can employers play in supporting NSmen in recognising their contributions towards Singapore's defence?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, can MINDEF also provide an update on what steps are being taken to ensure that NSmen receive recognition and are well taken care of in their service to the nation?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have led to serious spill-over effects around the world – ranging from disruptions to global supply chains to the rise of extremist violence.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must do more to preserve our social cohesion and economic resilience amid these volatile and uncertain times.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, Total Defence continues to play a critical role in building a strong, cohesive and resilient society, premised on every Singaporean playing a part to help our country overcome any crisis.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can MINDEF provide an update on efforts to involve Singaporeans in Total Defence, such as to encourage them to strengthen Social and Psychological Defence in their individual capacities?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In addition, how is MINDEF and the SAF helping Singaporeans to better understand its own efforts to strengthen Total Defence, such as through the formation of the new Digital and Intelligence Service, or the Republic of Singapore Navy's role in keeping sea lines of communication secure and open?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: The recent developments in the Middle East and Europe serve as a stark reminder of the ongoing importance of Total Defence and its six pillars.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: The proliferation of fake news and disinformation through various media channels has expanded the battlefield to encompass not only physical borders but also the hearts and minds of individuals.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: There is an urgent need for the active implementation of Total Defence among our populace.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: Despite Singapore's prolonged period of peace, the concept of Total Defence may still feel distant to many Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: While it is taught in schools, its practical implications on daily life may not always be evident.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: How can MINDEF encourage conversations among Singaporeans, to explore ways to incorporate Total Defence into their daily lives, thereby fostering a more resilient society?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Chairman, today's security challenges bear little resemblance to those of the past.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: These will have a profound and undesirable impact on our defence and security, as they seek to undermine our social fabric and weaken the resilience of our society.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: It is thus important for us to provide the platform for Singaporeans to understand the various defence and security issues as well as the roles they can play.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: It is also important to encourage Singaporeans to participate proactively in initiatives in bringing Total Defence into action.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: In particular, we should involve younger Singaporeans, who may not fully appreciate the extent of these developments and may find the topic of defence unfamiliar, distant and unrelatable.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: It is important to encourage their participation, so that we can nurture and tap on their potential to contribute in different areas of defence.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: When they have gained a deeper understanding, they would be more interested in how they can play a part in defending their homeland at different stages of their lives as they grow up.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: On this note, I would like to request MINDEF to elaborate on their efforts in ensuring that our youths are engaged on defence issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, in 2015's MINDEF Committee of Supplies debate, I had raised the issue of fair and equal deployment in the SAF, particularly in the vessels of the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In answering my previous question regarding having halal-certified kitchens on our vessels, the MINDEF Ministers had cited the key issue of space being a premium on ships and that other provision would be made not only for Muslim servicemen but any other services of other religions with dietary restrictions.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The video series was entertaining and educational on what midshipmen of both genders and races experienced during the MSTD.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe that it is important that we clearly communicate to the public – that there are no systemic barriers in the way of any Singaporean wishing to serve on our navy vessels.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Gaza strip are important lessons to Singaporeans – never to take peace for granted and to always be prepared to defend their nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Countries around the world have been racing to reverse their shrinking militaries by increasing defence spending and reinstating some form of national service.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For many of my contemporaries, we served NS because we felt the need to do our part to serve the nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But in today's world, there are many different narratives out in social media and fake news abound.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It will be more challenging for MINDEF to persuade Singaporeans to defend their country if there are external unfriendly forces trying to provide different reasons for aggression.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Photos and reports can be easily manipulated to paint a different picture for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These young men have just completed their "A" levels or polytechnic education and they come to collect their Edusave awards with neat, shaven haircut and in NS uniform.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Almost of all of them have a positive attitude towards NS and I wish to compliment MINDEF for a job well done.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But we should not rest on our laurels because NS and the defence of our nation is critical to our nation's survival.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can we do more to prepare our NSFs – for either a vocation or career after NS or to prepare them for their further studies?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I urge MINDEF to do more to allow our NSFs to feel that their time spent during NS is for the right purpose and that they have benefitted from their stint in NS.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East are grave reminders of the need for a strong defence of especially small nation states like Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The SAF was created from scratch in 1965, as a result of the need to build our own security capability.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We are blessed that political leaders like Mr Lee Kuan Yew and his team, including Dr Goh Keng Swee, had the foresight to build a strong SAF, bolstered by a robust conscription system.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This, in turn, is made possible by the willingness and strong support of Singaporeans who saw this national need.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Across generations since then, Singaporeans have played an important part in making personal sacrifices for the larger good of defending our nation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As the threats we face become increasingly complex in wars that are fought not only in the physical space but also in cyberspace, Singaporeans' commitment to a strong defence is now more important than ever.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The commitment and support of Singaporeans are really needed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For instance, are there avenues for women to serve in roles that are suitable for them and be recognised for their contributions?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, the Minister for Defence described the dynamic nature of the security threats that we face and highlighted the importance of building an SAF to meet these challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NS is the cornerstone of Singapore's defence and it is critical that we continue to strengthen its effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, I spoke about changes arising from the work of the NS Review Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We introduced measures to make the most of the contributions of NSmen to improve the NS experience and enhance the support for and recognition of NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I will provide an update on those initiatives as well as announce new ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Given low fertility rates, declining cohort sizes and an increasingly demanding mission, the SAF must continue to optimise the contributions of every NSman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how we are managing this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are doing so in two key ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: First, by reviewing medical fitness criteria and matching these to the physical requirements of jobs, we maximise the effective deployment of NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked about the assessments conducted for pre-enlistees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Functional assessments, which were introduced in January 2022 for pre-enlistees with selected orthopaedic conditions, assess their ability to perform the physical tasks required for the job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF has also continued to redesign job roles for NSFs by leveraging technology to assist with physical requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: More NSFs are then able to take on a wider range of roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Second, we invest in and tap on NSmen's skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: One example is through Work-Learn Schemes which Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With these, NSFs attain a diploma or partial university credits while performing a period of full-time NS followed by Regular service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This allows NSFs to fulfil their academic aspirations, put their learning into practice and contribute even better to the SAF with their enhanced skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since the first Cyber Work-Learn Scheme in 2018, we have expanded to domains such as engineering, supply chain management and artificial intelligence, and we will continue to explore additional domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: One, for NSFs to pursue Diplomas in Paramedic Science and be deployed as Army Medic Specialists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The other for officer or specialist cadets to serve as NSF Trainers, while gaining credits for an undergraduate degree with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about tapping on pre-enlistees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are partnering Singapore Polytechnic and the Republic Polytechnic to introduce new schemes for final-year diploma students to fulfil their internship requirements and enlist concurrently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With Singapore Polytechnic, we have launched the Polytechnic Cyber Work-Learn Scheme and the SAF-Polytechnic Sponsorship for Integrated Curriculum Diploma, or SPS-IC Diploma for Aerospace Electronics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With the Republic Polytechnic, we have launched the SPS-IC Diploma for Electrical and Electronic Engineering and another one for Information Technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Students taking cybersecurity or aerospace electronics courses with Singapore Polytechnic, or electrical and electronics engineering or IT courses with Republic Polytechnic are eligible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Those selected will serve for three to five years through a combination of full-time NS and Regular service as Cyber Specialists, or through full Regular service as Air Force Engineers or Naval Warfare System Experts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will expand this to other polytechnics and vocations in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our operationally-ready NSmen may also have developed niche skills beyond their full-time NS period, in their civilian careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since 2014, the SAF has been identifying NSmen with relevant skills and redeploying them to units where they can contribute their civilian expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked for an update.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to expand our efforts, having introduced marine survey as a new domain in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Maximising the operational readiness of NS personnel goes hand-in-hand with ensuring their safety and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Mohd Fahmi asked about training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are employing technology to improve performance while enhancing safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF has successfully tested using wearables to allow trainers to monitor the physiological data of soldiers in real-time and to calibrate fitness training accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This optimises training outcomes while enhancing safety supervision and minimising injury.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since April 2023, all SAF recruits have been issued wearables and heart rate zone-based training has been incorporated into their physical training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have also made good progress in developing a next-generation digital safety information system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Today, SAF units actively use the SafeGuardian app to submit near-misses and incident reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: All of this data is stored on the Enterprise Safety Information System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Units, such as the 1st Commando Battalion, have used insights from past trends to identify potential risk factors and adjust their training programmes accordingly to mitigate musculoskeletal injuries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Army has also used this data in a quarterly alert called PING, which stands for "Proactive Information to Nudge and Guide".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It compares each quarter's training activities with the preceding work year, so that units are aware of and can prevent common safety incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond technology, we regularly audit and review our safety systems and processes to ensure that they remain robust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Most recently, they completed system reviews to strengthen the training and qualification system for combat vehicle operators, and to enhance the safe conduct and management of inter-Service training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF also regularly benchmarks itself against external practices and standards through the work of the External Review Panel on SAF Safety (ERPSS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It continues to find strong command emphasis on training safety across the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They also noted the SAF's use of data in safety management and to prevent accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We appreciate the good work of ERPSS and the next term will commence soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will never let our guard down on safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Care for our servicemen also goes beyond ensuring their physical safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Ms He Ting Ru asked how MINDEF/SAF is looking at the mental wellness and well-being of our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF/SAF has in place efforts to promote effective self-care, strengthen coping skills and better recognise potential mental health issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: All Regulars and NSFs also undergo psychological first-aid training to help them recognise distress signs, exercise self-care and support their peers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have also continued our practice of screening for mental health conditions before enlistment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Those with severe conditions that pose harm to themselves or others are deferred from NS until they are professionally assessed to have improved and no longer pose those risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Those with mild or moderate conditions, but who have been assessed to be able to serve in selected vocations, will receive additional monitoring during NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond pre-enlistment screening, we have increased our mental health support over the years, particularly during Basic Military Training (BMT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Care Hubs have been set up in the BMT centres since 2020 so that mental health professionals and medical doctors can work closely with Commanders to support NSFs during their transition to military life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Commanders interview NSFs regularly to identify potential problems and to render assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I note that Ms He Ting Ru has also mentioned the importance of soldier moral strengths as well as resilience and how these will affect the effectiveness of the fighting units and fighting morale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is an important aspect and I can assure Ms He Ting Ru that through the use of appropriate instruments, not necessarily the ones that she particularly mentioned, we pick up signals of weakness, as well as discern strengths for better deployment and development of our servicemen for different vocations and for different levels of command.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We certainly want to press on with all efforts to make the most of the contributions of our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We understand also that Parliamentary Questions have been filed on this topic of mental health for our servicemen and we will give a more substantive reply at a subsequent Parliament Sitting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also continue to enhance the NS experience and improve administrative efficiency, so that our NSmen can focus on their NS duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about OneNS and the digitalisation of NS systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This web portal will be hosted on a commercial cloud platform and feature an improved design, allowing NSmen to access NS services more easily and with few disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Through OneNS, we aim to introduce a more personalised and engaging digital experience for all NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: OneNS is not just a web portal but a broader platform, including a mobile app that consolidates NS-related services and transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The app will make the daily routine more efficient for NSmen on In-Camp Training (ICT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen currently queue and scan their physical IDs for in-processing for ICT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Aside from the digital experience, we are also consolidating physical NS services for NSmen's greater convenience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about the progress of this one-stop location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Once completed, the building will bear the CMPB name because of its significance for multiple generations of NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This new CMPB will be an integrated service location for NS-related administration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen will be able to undergo the Health Screening Programme, take their IPPT or attend NS FIT training at the all-weather Fitness Conditioning Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They can then buy NS necessities at the Lifestyle mart located on-premise, or make use of the "Click and Collect" and "Pick and Pack" services if they so wish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Pre-enlistees will attend medical screening and take their pre-enlistment IPPT there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The medical screening time will be shortened, thanks to an easier registration process and improved sequencing of stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Enlistees, NSmen and the public can also look forward to amenities such as a food court, café, childcare centre, soccer field and fitness zone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We envisage these amenities to be open even on weekends, bringing convenience to NSmen and the community nearby.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The new CMPB will also be home to the SAF's second Regional Health Hub (RHH), which Miss Rachel Ong asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: RHHs consolidate the SAF's essential healthcare services under one roof for each region to provide even more responsive care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The first RHH serving the northwest region was officially opened in Kranji in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked how do we recognise the contributions of NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Examples include the NS Recognition Awards first introduced in the year 2010, which was subsequently enhanced into the NS HOME (Housing, Medical and Education) Awards in 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These awards support the NSmen's housing, healthcare and educational financing, and they are presented to NSmen in cash credits and top ups to their CPF and Post-Secondary Education Accounts at various milestones of their NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Good performance during NS is also recognised through the NS Excellence Awards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In addition, NSmen and their families receive tax relief every year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also celebrate our NSmen's life milestones with celebratory gifts of $100, when they solemnise their marriage, or welcome a child to the family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is on top of the $100 presented in 2022 to commemorate NS55.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These initiatives and others in this nature demonstrate and manifest and reflect MINDEF's continued strong emphasis on appreciating the valuable contributions of our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I note that Mr Neil Parekh also asked, "What about employers?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: How can employers also play a part in this?" Here, I want to record my thanks to the Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence (ACCORD).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have a council within the ACCORD on employers and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Through the work of that council, as well as broad employer groups and chambers, I think the message has really gone out to many employers that strong NS is synonymous with conditions to do good business in Singapore, because safety and security of this land enables proper business planning and investment decisions to be taken, for good business operations to be proceeded with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I think that over the years, more and more employers have understood this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: You can see this manifested in the increasing numbers of employers who have merited the NS Mark recognition as well as so many employers, who in their own ways, have made arrangements to support their NSmen when they have to report for their ICT, to recognise the leadership skills of the NSmen as they apply to their work, to recognise the relevant vocational skills like in logistics, like cyber, as they apply to those particular industries, for example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I want to thank these progressive employers for doing so and I hope that all employers can take a leaf from their book and also do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about the NS allowance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Instead of a salary, NSF receive an allowance to support their basic personal upkeep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: When we say that we will provide an allowance to support the basic upkeep of our NSFs, we mean it and we will ensure it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I note that Mr Giam has also used the word "obligation" in his cut – not wrong, but I also noted Dr Wan Rizal in his cut used the words "honour" and "duty" – also correct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are all on the same page because Mr Giam also finished his cut by saying that we all recognise the importance of citizens defending this country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Because for whom are we defending this country?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is for each and every Singaporean, for now and for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to review regularly to make sure that the allowance remains relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I spoke about the recognition packages, the ongoing allowances for our NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: There is something else which is that as they transit out of full-time NS into post-NSF life, many of them will either immediately or soon enough either further their studies or commence work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Therefore, we also pay close attention to ensuring that our NSFs' transition to employment is made as smooth as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Jean See asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: About 100 companies across a wide range of industries, such as food and beverage, retail and trade, health, energy and finance services, are already on board – and of course, every effort will be made to broaden this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSFs may apply to take advantage of the programme and strengthen their value in the labour market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Therefore, we care for NSFs not only during the full-time service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: When completed in 2027, it will again play host to major national events like the National Day Parade and bigger-scale community, sporting and recreational activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, NS remains the cornerstone in safeguarding our security, sovereignty and way of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We must continue to do our utmost to strengthen the NS system, to make full use of our NSFs' and NSmen's talents and skills, and to appreciate their valuable contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister for Defence Dr Ng and Senior Minister of State Mr Heng have updated the House on our efforts to ensure that the SAF remains effective and ready to defend Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To complement a strong SAF, Singapore needs a united and resilient population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For 40 years, Total Defence has continued to be relevant and has helped us navigate economic downturns, global uncertainties and even a recent pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we saw Singaporeans step forward to care for one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singaporeans delivered food and essential supplies to those who needed help, supported various COVID-19 measures, including vaccinations to protect our population, including seniors, and reminded one another to be discerning against fake news and misinformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about Total Defence lessons that we could learn from ongoing conflicts around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Even as we live in relative peace in Singapore, we must be prepared for threats that can disrupt our way of life and undermine our social identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Europe enjoyed decades of peace and many countries abolished conscription due to the "peace dividend".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Then, the Ukraine-Russia conflict happened – right at Europe's doorstep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Sweden and Finland quickly applied to join NATO.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The physical conflict in Gaza might be geographically far away from Singapore, but it has strong resonance and strong ripple effects on our population and our harmonious social fabric.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have seen how cyber hackers can attack energy infrastructure, as they did in Denmark, or disrupt public transport systems like they did in Poland.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These can affect public confidence and the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also seen the use of misinformation and hostile information campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Singapore must be ready for threats – both traditional and emerging ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, Total Defence is not just a concept or a narrative; it is imperative for all of us here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If and when crises and disruptions hit our shores, every one of us must play our part and stand ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked for an update on the exercise.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members can also access this through the SG PARL MP mobile app.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nearly 200 evacuation drills were conducted too, but rest assured none today, here in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These include students and educators from all over, 330 schools.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In some schools, students learnt about the value of water when they experienced water supply limitations during recess.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In response to a simulated food supply disruption, some secondary school students ate Ready-to-Eat meals from the Singapore Food Agency and SATS, while others learnt to make do with alternatives from a smaller range of food items, which were made available in their canteens.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: During simulated power disruptions, teachers adjusted their lesson activities to teach outside of classrooms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through these experiences, students said they better understood Singapore's vulnerabilities and the importance of being prepared and adaptable during times of disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the heartlands, residents adapted to simulated food and water disruptions and learnt about facilities essential for civic preparedness.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some residents went to alternate places for their groceries and meals when their neighbourhood markets and hawker centres were closed for market cleaning to simulate food disruptions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Over 200 households living in Yung Sheng Road adapted to water disruptions by collecting water from PUB's water wagon and water bag filling machines.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Visitors to community facilities such as the People's Association Integrated Community Hubs participated in evacuation drills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For instance, Pontiac Land Group, South Beach, Sofitel Singapore Sentosa Resort & Spa and others tested their business continuity plans in the event of a power failure.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Other companies conducted their own simulated cyber phishing exercises, referencing playbooks from the Cyber Security Agency, which were developed in consultation with Google and Microsoft.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I spoke to some of the CEOs and business owners, and they told me that the exercise was a timely one.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But what shone through was the spirit of care for fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thirty-five volunteers from Taman Jurong Community Emergency and Engagement Committee distributed water bags and made house calls during a simulated water disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Cheok Xin Lin, a nursing student at the National University of Singapore (NUS), was one of the volunteers and used his professional training to ensure that all residents and volunteers could participate in the exercise safely.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: He said that this exercise allowed them to test their contingency plans and help those in need.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It also helped them recognise that community support is crucial, as everyone had a part to play in times of crisis.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This year's Exercise SG Ready has provided just a slice of the disruptions that could hit us in a crisis.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It has prompted us to think about what we can do, how we can respond and why we must remain united.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am glad that it has resonated well with participants, and we will continue to find ways to educate, to activate, to think and to inspire action for Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Beyond the exercise, we will continue to engage Singaporeans on Total Defence throughout the year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Zulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Miss Rachel Ong asked about these efforts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We launched the Total Defence Exhibition which showcases examples of Singaporeans putting Total Defence in action.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through the exhibition, we hope that Singaporeans can reflect on the role that they play to keep Singapore strong and prepared.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Visitors are encouraged to make pledges in support of Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These pledges will be collated on a digital map of Singapore, showcasing Singaporeans' commitment to Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The exhibition is currently at the Singapore Discovery Centre and from March, it will move into several community spaces, including the National Library and SAFRA Choa Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This year, we also hope to bring the Total Defence community together.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The speakers will be both local and international and will provide perspectives around the theme of "Building Societal Resilience and Readiness in Disruptions and Crises".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our partners and practitioners will also have the opportunity to exchange best practises, network and discuss ideas through a series of workshops.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Beyond the programmes planned for TD40, we will continue to engage different groups of Singaporeans to strengthen Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about how MINDEF engages our youths.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Total Defence Sandbox (TD Sandbox) was launched in 2022 to call for ideas from Singaporeans on how the community can put Total Defence into action.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I spoke about this at MINDEF's COS debate last year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Initiated and developed by Finute – a Singapore-based metaverse edutainment company – this proposal taps on the online platform, Roblox, to create a Singapore within the metaverse.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Another group of students from NUS proposed an idea to strengthen Digital and Social Defence by harnessing the collective wisdom and skills of an online community of volunteers to identify scam websites, and raise awareness and understanding of scam detection.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are good ideas and MINDEF will continue to partner the community to implement them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, the theme of our Total Defence campaign this year is, "Together We Keep Singapore Strong".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our resilience and strength as a nation are dependent on each of us working together towards common goals.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Similarly, in the SAF, our servicemen and servicewomen are steadfast in their commitment to Singapore's military defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mr Faisal Manab asked about inclusiveness in the SAF.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The deployment of service personnel to vocations is based on merit, capability and aptitude, as well as their commitment to the SAF and to Singapore, regardless of race, gender or religion.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This approach is fair and optimises our manpower for SAF vocations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, we must not take the strong public affirmation for granted.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will continue to raise community awareness about the importance of NS and defence, as Ms Denise Phua and Mr Lim Biow Chuan highlighted.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One of our efforts is through the Advisory Council on Community Relations and in Defence (ACCORD), which like Total Defence, is turning 40 this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, ACCORD continues to run a wide range of community outreach initiatives to reach out to pre-enlistees, youths, new citizens, Permanent Residents (PRs), NSmen, families and women.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some Members of Parliament such as Member He Ting Ru, Mr Zulkarnain Rahim and Mr Don Wee are also active members of ACCORD.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The goal is to bring society together, to champion and to advocate for Singapore's defence and for NS.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: ACCORD initiated NS info-sharing sessions with pre-enlistees, including those who are new citizens and PRs, to better ease their transition into military life.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: ACCORD also initiated the NS Family Camp in partnership with SAFRA, where families built barshas with full camouflage on and even belted out familiar military tunes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Supporting our NSmen in their professional development is another key tenet of ACCORD's work.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under these MOUs, our NSmen enjoy concessionary rates for selected programmes to upskill, reskill and learn relevant security and Human Resource knowledge.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked about the role of employers in supporting our NSmen in recognition of their contributions towards the defence of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The best form of employer support for our NSmen is to support their NS commitments.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For instance, some employers introduce flexible work arrangements before in-camp training or celebrate our NSmen's NS achievements during company events.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are heartened to see that in the same IPS survey, 95% of employed NSmen respondents agreed that their employers were supportive of their NS commitments.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I thank employers too for their support.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Denise Phua also asked about the role of women in defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, women are already contributing to our military defence as Regulars and volunteers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members might also be familiar with another ACCORD initiative, the Women's Boot Camp, which started in 2018 to provide women with a glimpse of NS life through participation in Basic Military Training activities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The experience has inspired some to even consider a career in the SAF.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We continue to reach out to women to be our advocates for NS and defence and encourage them to do their part wherever they can.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, reflecting on the past 40 years of Total Defence, we find a journey marked by strength, resilience and a collective commitment by Singaporeans to safeguard our home and our way of life.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Over the decades, we have continuously evolved our approach to Total Defence to adapt to evolving challenges.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Yet, amidst all these challenges, what endures is the unwavering spirit of Total Defence and the understanding that everyone has a part to play.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As we move forward, let us remember that keeping Singapore strong is a shared responsibility, not just during crises and disruptions, but also during peacetime.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Together, let us keep Singapore strong for many generations to come.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: The Senior Minister of State said that NS is a duty to country and is not employment.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: However, does the Senior Minister of State agree that the two are not mutually exclusive?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: For example, SAF regulars, they are both employees and they are also serving their national duty.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But that does not detract in any way their sense of national duty.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I want to emphasise that I do support NS, but I feel that NS pay should better reflect the realities of the opportunity costs that NSmen have to incur.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Giam for his question.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I think we agree that serving NS to protect this country is a duty of citizens.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: That is why we recognise that in the fulfilment of their duty, we also provide for this basic upkeep.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: And this is also why we regularly update and enhance the allowance that we so pay to our NSFs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I would just like to repeat my request: whether the Senior Minister of State can provide an update regarding the steps and measures taken thus far in making RSN naval vessels a more inclusive and open workspace?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have given him replies on this issue previously and the considerations have not changed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The provision of halal food requires adherence to religious stipulations, including on the food source, preparation and storage.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For local training and operations – that is, trainings in Singapore – these conditions can be met by having separate kitchens and halal-certified sources of food.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The SAF also provides halal food to our soldiers in camps or when they are training outdoors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But when SAF soldiers are deployed overseas, there are practical constraints.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For overseas exercises on land, the SAF links up with local suppliers to provide halal food where feasible.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And depending on the country that they are training in.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: You have to understand that the landscape is very different from having our cookhouses here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On Navy ships, the kitchens need to be self-sufficient to prepare and provide meals for all servicemen on board – not just the Muslim servicemen, but also others who may have other dietary restrictions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The space for kitchens and storage of food needs to be compact and maximised due to other operational constraints, such as control and combat systems, ammunition and equipment spares, as well as living quarters for our servicemen.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have to separate the kitchen from the food being served – two different things.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For our Muslim personnel on board our ships, our ships provide options, such as seafood, chicken and vegetables.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I note that Mr Faisal Manap noted seeing our Malay serviceman in our video.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For non-Muslim Navy personnel with specific dietary restrictions, such as vegetarians, they can also select from these options on the ships too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think we have to basically consider that there are different considerations for different groups and we have operational considerations as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nonetheless, we thank all our servicemen and servicewomen, particularly those on ships and when training overseas, who understand these constraints and accept them.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think it is heartening to note that MINDEF is investing regularly and steadily, to keep our defence strong.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In order for Total Defence to work, things like these probably need to be done regularly and institutionalised.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I just wanted to check whether that is the plan and to get more organisations involved in understanding their roles?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Because indeed, it is not just within these few weeks that we engage these organisations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are all a collection of activities, events to commemorate the importance of Total Defence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What is more important is Singaporeans coming onboard and practising it daily, because we always have to be conscious.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope that the experience, whether they are in school, whether they are part of a company, is something that is memorable and that people remember of some of the threats that are always around us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One thing I reckon, as Minister Ng said yesterday, is that Singaporeans understand our vulnerabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, there is a certain acceptance that we have to be united because the threats are not just within here.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The threats are coming from outside, and we have to be united and resilient as a society.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this is where Total Defence will play a role across all our six pillars.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And I thank the Member for his support.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Any other Members have clarifications for the Ministers?

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, can I invite Mr Vikram Nair to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: My thanks to the Minister and two Senior Ministers of State for their sharing and for all our serving people in the armed forces and reservists.
